_comment: English texts of the engine messages (crates/engine-msg). Key: area.topic.name. Placeholders: {name}, filled with a number and its unit, a name, or another message of this catalog. The app shows them in the user language from apps/web/src/i18n/engine/<tag>.json.
depot.cannot_turn: A {vehicle} cannot turn into lanes at {angle}° even with a 40 m aisle.
depot.draw_zone: Draw a parking or charging zone for the auto layout to fill.
depot.lane.no_aisle_entry: No aisle in front of the lane entry.
depot.lane.no_aisle_exit: No aisle in front of the lane exit.
depot.lane.no_room_in: The turn into the lane does not fit: the lane is too short for the turn.
depot.lane.no_room_out: The turn out of the lane does not fit.
depot.lane.obstacle_in: Driving in, the vehicle would touch a parked vehicle.
depot.lane.obstacle_out: Driving out, the vehicle would touch a parked vehicle.
depot.lane.outside_in: Driving in, the vehicle would run over the depot fence.
depot.lane.outside_out: Driving out, the vehicle would run over the depot fence.
depot.lane.too_sharp: The lane meets its aisle at more than 100°.
depot.lane_dropped: 1 lane was left out because a vehicle could not turn into or out of it without touching the fence or a parked vehicle.
depot.lanes_dropped: {count} lanes were left out because a vehicle could not turn into or out of them without touching the fence or a parked vehicle.
depot.no_charger: {group}: {count} battery vehicles park without a charger.
depot.no_drive_both: No drive from an entrance to this lane, nor from it to an exit.
depot.no_drive_in: No drive from an entrance to this lane.
depot.no_drive_out: No drive from this lane to an exit.
depot.no_entrance: The depot has no entrance: add a gate.
depot.no_exit: The depot has no exit: add a gate.
depot.no_lane_fits: No lane fits: a lane of {length} m by {width} m with {aisle} m aisles on both ends does not fit in this zone.
depot.no_slot_fits: {group}: {short} of {count} vehicles have no slot that fits them ({length} m long).
depot.no_slots: The depot has no slots yet: draw zones and run the auto layout.
depot.straight_drives: Drives inside the depot run in straight lines through open space; draw a circulation zone or leave room along the fence where vehicles should drive.
depot.vehicle_unknown: {group}: its vehicle is unknown to the depot.
gtfs.unknown_route_types: Route types {types} are not known and are read as bus.
gtfs.untimed_trips: {count} trips without times were left out.
journey.route_unlisted: Route {route} is not listed; shown by its id.
journey.stop_twice: Stop {stop} is listed twice; the first entry is used.
journey.transfer_unknown_stop: Transfer {from} → {to} names an unknown stop; ignored.
journey.trip_back_in_time: Trip {trip} goes back in time; skipped.
journey.trip_unknown_stop: Trip {trip} calls at unknown stop {stop}; skipped.
kits.berth.conflict: Vessels wait for a berth at {pier} {holds} times in {window} minutes (in total {held}). Add a berth or change the headway or layover.
kits.call.unknown_pier: A call refers to a pier that no longer exists.
kits.capacity.ceiling_cabin: {capacity} passengers per hour and direction is more than any ropeway carries (about {ceiling}).
kits.capacity.ceiling_train: {capacity} passengers per hour and direction is more than any people mover carries (about {ceiling}).
kits.clearance.min_cabin: The loaded cabin comes within {clearance} of the ground; at least {min} is needed.
kits.clearance.min_train: The underside of the guideway comes within {clearance} of the ground; at least {min} is needed.
kits.clearance.recommended_cabin: The loaded cabin comes within {clearance} of the ground; {recommended} is recommended.
kits.clearance.recommended_train: The underside of the guideway comes within {clearance} of the ground; {recommended} is recommended.
kits.dwell.over_capacity: {pax} passengers on and off at a call is more than the vessel carries ({capacity}).
kits.ground.assumed_all: Ground is a straight line between the station heights. Terrain and building heights are not checked.
kits.ground.assumed_section: No terrain heights for this section; the ground is a straight line between the station heights.
kits.leg.same_pier: Two calls in a row at the same pier.
kits.line.too_short_piers: Click at least two piers on the map.
kits.line.too_short_stations: Click at least two stations on the map.
kits.route.unchecked: The route follows your via points. Land, bridges, locks and water depth are not checked yet.
kits.span.too_long_cabin: Span {span} is {length}; this system spans at most {max}. Add a tower.
kits.span.too_long_train: Span {span} is {length}; this system spans at most {max}. Add a pier.
kits.station.angle: The line turns {angle}° here; this system allows {max}° in a station.
kits.station.angle_reversible_cabin: An aerial tramway runs straight; it turns {angle}° here. Split it into two lines.
kits.station.angle_reversible_train: A cable-hauled shuttle runs straight; it turns {angle}° here. Split it into two lines.
kits.station.intermediate_reversible_cab: Aerial tramways rarely have stations between the terminals; both cabins stop when one does.
kits.station.intermediate_reversible_tra: Shuttles rarely have stations between the terminals; both trains stop when one does.
kits.tower.too_tall_cabin: A tower {at} along is {height} tall; this system's towers are at most {max}.
kits.tower.too_tall_train: A pier {at} along is {height} tall; this system's piers are at most {max}.
kits.zone.busy: The fleet is busy {busy} % of the time, above the {target} % that keeps waits short; {needed} vehicles are recommended.
kits.zone.crossing: The zone's outline crosses itself. Move a point so the outline goes round once.
kits.zone.draw: Click at least three points on the map to outline the zone.
kits.zone.fleet_short: {fleet} vehicles cannot keep up with {requests} requests an hour: about {needed} are needed.
kits.zone.full: Vehicles carry {riders} riders on average with {places} places: many requests would find them full.
kits.zone.hours: The service ends before it starts.
kits.zone.no_fleet: Set how many vehicles serve the zone.
kits.zone.wait: Riders wait about {wait} min on average, more than the {max} min recommended.
noise.check.bridge: Elevated over {length}: bridge structure noise {db} dB ({low} to {high} dB, CNOSSOS-EU bridge transfer functions)
noise.check.electric_buses: Electric buses: propulsion noise {db} dB ({low} to {high} dB), an educated guess until measured values are added
noise.check.lden_widest: The {threshold} L_den band is widest here: {distance} from the line
noise.check.no_night: No night service: no {threshold} L_night band
noise.check.quick_estimate: Quick estimate: free field over flat ground, no buildings or terrain (no screening), service lines only without general traffic
noise.check.source_berth: Ferries at the pier: placeholder sound power, no source yet: indicative only
noise.check.source_cable_car: Cable cars: sound powers from one study (Placer County gondola EIR, 2019): indicative
noise.check.source_ferry: Ferries under way: sound power from one study of large ferries (port of Livorno, Fredianelli and Nastasi 2020): indicative
noise.check.source_small_vessel: Water buses, catamarans and hydrofoils under way: placeholder sound power, no source for small vessels yet: indicative only
noise.check.squeal: Curve R {radius} over {length}: squeal correction {db} dB ({low} to {high} dB), the corridor widens here
noise.check.squeal_tram: Tram curve R {radius} over {length}: squeal correction {db} dB ({low} to {high} dB), the corridor widens here
noise.check.switch_impact: {count} switches: impact noise {db} dB from {extent} before to {extent} after each
noise.check.switch_impact_one: 1 switch: impact noise {db} dB from {extent} before to {extent} after each
noise.check.switch_slow: {count} switches: no impact noise below {speed} km/h (CNOSSOS-EU)
noise.check.switch_slow_one: 1 switch: no impact noise below {speed} km/h (CNOSSOS-EU)
noise.check.underground: {length} underground: no noise at the surface; tunnel portals are not modelled yet
rail.alignment.radius_below_minimum: Curve radius {radius} is below the {minimum} minimum for {what}.
rail.alignment.radius_below_minimum_sque: Curve radius {radius} is below the {minimum} minimum for {what} (not enough room between the points).
rail.alignment.radius_below_recommended: Curve radius {radius} is below the recommended {recommended}; trains slow to {speed} here.
rail.alignment.ramp_not_clear: Not enough clear length to go from {from} to {to}: the ramp needs {ramp} at {gradient}, but only {clear} is clear of switches ({start} to {end} along the track). Move the switch or lengthen the track.
rail.alignment.ramp_too_long: Not enough length to go from {from} to {to}: the ramp needs {ramp} at {gradient} with {vertical_radius} vertical curves, but the track is {length} long ({short} short). Lengthen the track or move a level change to a station further away.
rail.alignment.ramps_overlap: Two level changes overlap (ramps of {first} and {second}). Move the points further apart.
rail.alignment.turn_too_sharp: Turn too sharp to fit a curve. Move the point or add one more.
rail.area.distant: the approach to a main signal
rail.area.storage_exit: the exit of a storage track
rail.crossing.diamond: Diamond crossing at {angle} on {level}: the two tracks share one piece of trackwork.
rail.crossing.diamond_too_flat: Diamond crossing too flat ({angle}). The catalogue's flattest diamond is {ratio}.
rail.crossing.flat_high_speed: Flat crossing with a high-speed track. Make one track a flyover or a dive-under.
rail.crossing.gauges_differ: {mode} ({gauge} mm) and {other} ({other_gauge} mm) cross on one level with different gauges: the diamond needs a special frog for each gauge and a lower speed over it.
rail.crossing.overhead_systems: The overhead lines of {mode} ({supply}) and {other} ({other_supply}) cross: the crossing needs an insulated crossing of the contact wires with a neutral section.
rail.crossing.ramp_same_height: Two tracks cross on a ramp at the same height. Change one track's level.
rail.crossing.shared_diamond: {mode} and {other} cross at {angle} on {level}: one shared diamond with sleepers under both systems' rails. Only one train at a time may occupy it, from either line.
rail.design.all_ok: No sharp corners or impossible connections: every curve meets the minimum radius, every switch is a catalogue element on straight track, every level change has a ramp within the maximum gradient.
rail.existing.gauge_differs: {track} joins {existing}, but its gauge ({gauge}) differs from the existing track ({existing_gauge}). Trains cannot run from one to the other: use the existing gauge, dual gauge track, or keep the lines apart.
rail.existing.join_angle: {track} meets {existing} at {angle}. A turnout leaves the existing track at a few degrees: draw the new track so it runs alongside the existing one where it joins.
rail.existing.joins: {track} joins {existing}: a new turnout goes into the existing track there.
rail.existing.level_crossing: This track crosses {existing} on the same level, at {angle}. That needs a diamond crossing built into the existing track and an interlocking shared with its operator. Take the new track over or under it.
rail.existing.on_top: This track lies on top of {existing} for {length}. The track is already there: join the existing track instead of drawing it again, or move the new track beside it.
rail.existing.other_system: {track} joins {existing}, a different railway system ({mode} track joining {existing_mode}). Through running needs vehicles built for both, such as tram-trains, and matching platforms and signalling.
rail.existing.power_differs: {track} joins {existing}, which is {power}, unlike this track. Trains running through need to change power system (dual-system or battery vehicles), and the join needs a system separation section.
rail.existing.tram_crossing: This track crosses {existing} on the level, at {angle}: a diamond crossing goes into the existing track.
rail.plan.cannot_move: {run}: the train cannot move at {position} (too little tractive effort for the gradient?)
rail.plan.cannot_move_here: the train cannot move at {position} (too little tractive effort for the gradient?)
rail.plan.cannot_run_outbound: Track joins the stops in the line's direction, but trains cannot run along it: {reason}.
rail.plan.cannot_run_return: Track joins the stops in the return direction, but trains cannot run along it: {reason}.
rail.plan.cannot_wait: the train cannot wait in its platform that long
rail.plan.leaves_earlier: {run} leaves earlier by {by} to keep clear of another train.
rail.plan.leaves_later: {run} leaves later by {by} to keep clear of another train.
rail.plan.next_train_late: the next train on {track} is not back there in time
rail.plan.no_free_train: No train was free to start some trips: trains cannot turn at the terminal named above, or its platforms are full. Add a crossover before the terminal so trains reach the departure platform, or a storage track joined to it; a storage track that only reaches the arrival platform does not help.
rail.plan.no_overnight_from_siding: no overnight track with room is reachable from the end-station siding
rail.plan.no_run_built: no run can be built from {track} to {to}
rail.plan.no_stabling_reaches: no stabling track reaches a free first platform
rail.plan.no_stabling_reaches_at: no stabling track reaches a free first platform at {station}
rail.plan.no_stabling_room: no stabling track with room is reachable
rail.plan.no_storage_reaches: No storage track reaches {stations}: the line's trains can only stay overnight in the terminal platforms, so it runs with few trains. Join a storage track to the line with a switch both ways, or check the signals between them.
rail.plan.no_track_outbound: No track connects the stops in the line's direction. Check that the stations are joined by track in the order of the stops.
rail.plan.no_track_return: No track connects the stops in the return direction. Check that the stations are joined by track in the order of the stops.
rail.plan.no_train_for_siding: no overnight track has a train to bring to the end-station siding {track} in time
rail.plan.no_way_on: a train from {track} reaches {to} with no way on to start the trip
rail.plan.path_misses_platform: the path does not run along platform {platform}
rail.plan.platform_changes: At {station}, {count} trips used another platform than usual.
rail.plan.platform_changes_one: At {station}, 1 trip used another platform than usual.
rail.plan.shifted: {count} departures moved from the clock-face times to keep clear of other trains.
rail.plan.shifted_one: 1 departure moved from the clock-face times to keep clear of other trains.
rail.plan.stalls_after: the train stalls on a gradient too steep for it after {from}, about {distance} after {from}. The track checks warn where the track is steeper than the maximum: change the level there, or the heights of the station and track
rail.plan.stalls_between: the train stalls on a gradient too steep for it between {from} and {to}, about {distance} after {from}. The track checks warn where the track is steeper than the maximum: change the level there, or the heights of the station and track
rail.plan.storage_full: every storage track is in use ({tracks}): add storage tracks, or a siding at the end station
rail.plan.storage_full_at: every storage track is in use ({tracks}): add storage tracks, or a siding at {station}
rail.plan.storage_no_exit_signal: The {track} has no signal to leave by, so its trains cannot come out. A signal at its exit (in front of the switch that joins it to the line) lets them out.
rail.plan.trains_in_the_way: Trains get in each other's way on the track. Crossovers next to the terminals let trains turn without blocking the other track; otherwise run less often.
rail.plan.way_out_taken: the way out of {place} is taken at the departure
rail.signal.inside_area: Signal {signal} stands inside {area}. A train stopped at it blocks {area} for every other train. Move it to the edge, before it.
rail.signal.line_of_sight: Trams drive on sight, so signal {signal} does not let them follow each other closer. It is only needed in front of switches and crossings.
rail.signal.next_too_close: The next signal is only {distance} beyond signal {signal}, less than the {braking} a train needs to stop from {speed}. A train passing signal {signal} cannot stop at the next one if it shows stop. Move them apart, or announce it with a distant signal.
rail.signal.not_main: Signal {signal} protects {area} but is not a main signal, so it cannot set a route into it. Make it a main signal.
rail.signal.off_track: Signal {signal} is no longer on a track (its track, station or switch changed). Delete it, or reset the signals.
rail.signal.previous_too_close: Signal {signal} is only {distance} beyond the signal before it, less than the {braking} a train needs to stop from {speed}. Move them apart, or announce it with a distant signal.
rail.signal.removed_area: No signal in front of {area}: the generated signal there was removed. Trains are not stopped before {area}, so one can run into a train crossing it. Reset the signals, or place a signal at the edge of {area}.
rail.signal.removed_block: A block signal was removed: the block grows to {block} where {enough} is enough at {speed}. Trains must keep further apart, so fewer fit per hour. Reset the signals, or place a block signal there.
rail.signal.removed_distant: A distant signal was removed: trains get no warning that the main signal ahead may show stop, so they must approach it slowly enough to stop on sight. Reset the signals, or place a distant signal at braking distance before it.
rail.signal.removed_speed: A speed signal was removed: the drop to {speed} is not signed, so a driver may run into it too fast. Reset the signals, or place a speed signal there.
rail.signal.removed_starter: No starter signal at the end of a platform track: the generated one was removed. Trains cannot be held at the platform, so the line ahead is not protected. Reset the signals, or place a main signal at the platform end.
rail.signal.removed_storage_exit: No signal at the exit of a storage track: the generated one was removed. Trains put away there have no signal to leave by, so they cannot come out. Reset the signals, or place a shunting signal where the storage track joins the line.
rail.signal.splits_line: Signal {signal} splits the line, so trains can follow each other closer and more fit per hour.
rail.signal.splits_line_blocks: Signal {signal} splits the line into blocks of {behind} and {ahead}, so trains can follow each other closer and more fit per hour.
rail.signal.train_reaches_back: A {train} train stopped at signal {signal} reaches back into {area}, so it blocks it while it waits. Move the signal further on, or take it out.
rail.slip.lost_crossing: A slip lost its crossing: the tracks crossing there changed. Choose the slip again in the crossing list.
rail.slip.main_line_element: {slip} is a main line element, not usually built for {mode} track.
rail.slip.needs_one_level: A slip needs the two tracks to cross on one level.
rail.slip.needs_straight: {slip} needs straight track for {length} each side of the crossing. Move the curves away from it.
rail.slip.not_a_slip: {element} is not a slip in the catalogue.
rail.slip.one_system: {slip} joins tracks of one railway system; here {mode} crosses {other}.
rail.slip.single_tracks: {slip} joins two single tracks. Where double tracks cross, use a double junction or a crossover instead.
rail.slip.turn_between: {what} ({slip}): trains can also turn between the two tracks here.
rail.slip.turn_between_speed: {what} ({slip}): trains can also turn between the two tracks here at up to {speed}.
rail.slip.wrong_angle: {slip} is built for tracks crossing at {ratio} ({angle}). These tracks cross at {actual_ratio} ({actual_angle}): change the angle between them.
rail.station.platform_short: {station}: platform {platform} is too short for a {train} train plus {tolerance} stopping tolerance.
rail.station.terminus_no_crossover_ahead: {station} ahead end is a terminus with no crossover on the approach: trains cannot change track to turn back.
rail.station.terminus_no_crossover_rear: {station} rear end is a terminus with no crossover on the approach: trains cannot change track to turn back.
rail.street.crosses_ramp: {name} crosses the track on its ramp, where the track is neither at street level nor deep or high enough to pass under or over the street. Move the ramp away from the street.
rail.street.cycle_angle: {name} crosses the track at {angle}, flatter than {limit}: a bicycle wheel can drop into the gap beside the rail and the rider falls. Bend the path so it meets the track nearer a right angle.
rail.street.flat_angle: {name} crosses the track at {angle}, flatter than {limit}: the crossing is long and drivers cannot see along the line. Cross nearer to a right angle.
rail.street.how.barriers: barriers close the street {warning} before a train ({distance} before the crossing at {speed})
rail.street.how.marked: a marked crossing with warning signs, where people look out for the tram
rail.street.how.path_gates: lights and pedestrian gates or a maze close the path {warning} before a train
rail.street.how.traffic_signals: traffic signals stop road traffic for the tram
rail.street.level_crossing: Level crossing with {name} at {angle}: {how}. Buses and other road vehicles wait {distance} from the crossing point and never stop on the track.
rail.street.line_speed: The line speed over the level crossing with {name} is {speed}, above the usual limit of {limit}. It needs full barriers with obstacle detection tied to the signals, so trains stop while the crossing is not clear, or a lower speed there.
rail.street.mode_no_crossing_path: {mode} track crosses {name} on the level. {mode} lines normally have no level crossings. This one needs full barriers, obstacle detection and train protection that stops trains while the crossing is not clear. Consider a footbridge or an underpass.
rail.street.mode_no_crossing_street: {mode} track crosses {name} on the level. {mode} lines normally have no level crossings. This one needs full barriers, obstacle detection and train protection that stops trains while the crossing is not clear. Consider taking the track under or over the street.
rail.street.motorway: {name} is a motorway, and motorways normally have no level crossings. This one needs full barriers across every lane, obstacle detection and advance warning signs and signals well before the crossing. Consider a bridge.
rail.street.path_crossing: Path crossing with {name} for {users} at {angle}: {how}. They wait {distance} from the crossing point.
rail.street.third_rail: This track crosses {name} on the level with a third rail, which would be live where road vehicles and people cross. It needs a gap in the third rail across the crossing (trains coast over it) with insulated ends and fencing, or overhead line on this stretch.
rail.street.trolley_ac: The trolleybus wires on {name} cannot cross the railway's overhead line ({system}): trolleybuses lower their poles and cross on battery here.
rail.street.trolley_dc: The trolleybus wires on {name} cross the railway's overhead line ({system}): this needs an insulated crossing of the trolleybus and railway wires.
rail.street_running.cyclists_rails: Cyclists on {name} ride along the tram rails: a wheel caught in the groove is a common cause of falls. A bike lane beside the track (GIS tab) keeps them off the rails.
rail.street_running.mixed_bus_narrow: in the traffic lanes, shared with cars and buses: the street is about {width} wide and a tram lane with road lanes beside it needs {needed}
rail.street_running.mixed_bus_set: in the traffic lanes, shared with cars and buses (set in the GIS tab)
rail.street_running.mixed_main_road: The tram runs {length} along {name} {how}. On a main road the tram is held up in traffic jams and can be stuck in gridlock, so it runs late (about {delay} longer here at peak). Give it its own lane, separated from the traffic, in the GIS tab (move parking or a road lane), or use traffic signals that let the tram go first.
rail.street_running.mixed_narrow: in the traffic lanes, shared with cars: the street is about {width} wide and a tram lane with road lanes beside it needs {needed}
rail.street_running.mixed_set: in the traffic lanes, shared with cars (set in the GIS tab)
rail.street_running.own_lane: in its own lane ({width}), with a road lane each way beside it
rail.street_running.own_lane_separated_s: in its own lane, separated from the traffic (set in the GIS tab)
rail.street_running.own_lane_set: in its own lane (set in the GIS tab)
rail.street_running.painted_lane: The tram runs {length} along {name} {how}. The lane is only painted, so turning, parking and loading cars still get in the way (about {delay} longer here at peak); a kerb or separate track bed (separation in the GIS tab) keeps them out.
rail.street_running.painted_lane_limited: The tram runs {length} along {name} {how}, at up to {limit} (the street's speed limit). The lane is only painted, so turning, parking and loading cars still get in the way (about {delay} longer here at peak); a kerb or separate track bed (separation in the GIS tab) keeps them out.
rail.street_running.runs_along_limited: The tram runs {length} along {name} {how}, at up to {limit} (the street's speed limit).
rail.street_running.stop_island: Tram stop {stop} on {name} has an island platform in the middle of the street: passengers reach it over the road lanes, so it needs a signalled pedestrian crossing at its end.
rail.street_running.stop_kerb: Tram stop {stop} on {name}: passengers board from the pavement (a kerb stop), and road traffic waits behind the tram while it stands at the stop.
rail.street_running.stop_platforms: Tram stop {stop} on {name}: passengers board from platforms beside the tracks.
rail.switch.built_with_legs: {switch}: built with {built} because the legs of {chosen} cannot meet at {spacing} track centres.
rail.switch.built_with_scissors: {switch}: built with {built} because two crossovers in a row with {chosen} do not fit on the straight track here.
rail.switch.crossover_needs_double: Crossovers join the two tracks of a double track.
rail.switch.in_spread: {name} is where the tracks spread towards the platforms. Move it onto parallel track.
rail.switch.incomplete_geometry: {element} is not a turnout with complete geometry.
rail.switch.junction_needs_double: A double junction needs a double track.
rail.switch.on_curve: {name} sits on a curve. Catalogue switches go on straight track.
rail.switch.on_ramp: {name} is on a ramp. Switches should not sit on a gradient change or vertical curve.
rail.switch.overlap: Two switches overlap. Move one along the track.
rail.switch.past_end: {name} runs past the end of the track.
rail.switch.too_close: {name}: the tracks are {spacing} apart, too close for the catalogue turnouts' legs to meet. Use a flatter turnout, or widen the track spacing.
rail.terrain.station_height: {station} is level with its rails at {rail} above sea level; the ground along it lies between {low} and {high}.
rail.terrain.station_street_falls: {height} At street level the ground falls {fall} along the station, so the street round it has to be regraded by up to {regrade}. Move the station to flatter ground or build it elevated or underground.
rail.terrain.steep_ground: The ground is this steep here. Change the level (elevated or underground) or route the track along the slope. Heights come from a surface model, so buildings and trees can still show through.
rail.terrain.steep_tie_in: Part of it comes from meeting the level station or the switch at the end of the track; give the track more length there or move the station.
rail.terrain.street_track_above: Street-level track runs up to {height} above the ground over {length} to meet the level station or switch at its end (tolerance {tolerance}). The street has to be regraded here; move the station or change the level.
rail.terrain.street_track_below: Street-level track runs up to {height} below the ground over {length} to meet the level station or switch at its end (tolerance {tolerance}). The street has to be regraded here; move the station or change the level.
rail.terrain.track_climbs: The track climbs at up to {gradient} over {length} (km {from}–{to}); the maximum is {max}. {why}
rail.terrain.track_falls: The track falls at up to {gradient} over {length} (km {from}–{to}); the maximum is {max}. {why}
rail.track.clearance: Tracks of two alignments only {distance} apart; they need at least {needed} between track centres (clearance marker).
rail.track.joins_other_system_station: This {mode} track joins a {other} station. They are separate railway systems; join tracks of one system, or let them cross.
rail.track.joins_other_system_switch: This {mode} track joins a {other} switch. They are separate railway systems; join tracks of one system, or let them cross.
rail.track.lost_end: This track lost its end connection (the station or its tracks changed). Drag the end onto a connection point.
rail.track.lost_start: This track lost its start connection (the station, its tracks or the switch changed). Delete it or draw it again.
rail.track.open_end: Open track end. Connect it to a station or a switch, or set the track to storage to end it at a buffer stop.
rail.track.open_start: Open track start. Connect it to a station or a switch, or set the track to storage to end it at a buffer stop.
rail.track.storage_short_unnamed: Storage track holds {length}, shorter than one {train} train.
rail.track.through_station: This track runs through station {station} on the same level. Connect it to the station's tracks, or change its level.
street.depot.no_entrance_gate: The depot has no entrance gate.
street.depot.no_exit_gate: The depot has no exit gate.
street.depot.no_path: No legal path between the depot and this terminal.
street.depot.terminal_off_road: The terminal stop is not on a usable road.
street.line.beyond_battery: {length} without overhead wire exceeds the battery range of {range}.
street.line.end_stops: More than two end stops. A route has one end stop (circular line) or two (two directions); use a pattern for short turns.
street.line.mixed_traffic: The line runs {length} in the traffic of main roads: traffic jams and gridlock hold the buses up, about {delay} per round at peak, and they run late. Give these streets a bus lane in the GIS tab, separated from the traffic to keep cars out of it.
street.line.mixed_traffic_along: The line runs {length} in the traffic of main roads ({streets}): traffic jams and gridlock hold the buses up, about {delay} per round at peak, and they run late. Give these streets a bus lane in the GIS tab, separated from the traffic to keep cars out of it.
street.line.mixed_traffic_along_more: The line runs {length} in the traffic of main roads ({streets} and {more} more): traffic jams and gridlock hold the buses up, about {delay} per round at peak, and they run late. Give these streets a bus lane in the GIS tab, separated from the traffic to keep cars out of it.
street.line.no_legal_path: No legal path: one-way streets, turn bans or vehicle limits block it, and buses may not U-turn. Move a point or put the end stop where the vehicle can turn (bus station, loop, roundabout).
street.line.no_road_near: No road usable by this vehicle within {distance}.
street.line.not_on_road: It is not on a usable road.
street.line.on_battery: Runs {length} on battery without overhead wire.
street.line.red_legs: Some legs cannot be driven; see the red legs.
street.line.turning_detour: Turning round adds {extra} ({length} instead of {direct}). Consider putting the end stop where the vehicle can turn: a bus station, turning loop, roundabout or a block it can drive round.
street.line.two_stops: A line needs at least two stops. Promote points to stops.
street.line.wrong_side: This leg is {length} for {straight} in a straight line. If the next point is on the far half of a divided road, or on a one-way street the wrong way, move it to the side the vehicle drives on.
street.line.wrong_sidewalk: This sidewalk cannot be served: traffic here only runs with the stop on the far side from the doors. Put the stop on the other sidewalk.
